messages:
yara: Heads-up  I'd like to propose a "minimal handover" package for private deploys (VPC + on-prem) that the field can drop into customer netops without follow-ups. Aim: reduce back-and-forth and make upgrades predictable.

owen: Love the idea. Can we standardize a small artifact set (peering manifest, signed installer blob, and a validation bundle)? Also suggest a short 'SME contact card' the customer can call during the window.

claire: From product POV: minimal GA should guarantee two things: (1) documented peering handshake with a tokenized exchange (no long-lived console creds), (2) an upgrade path that either preserves customer-facing IPs or explicitly documents the cloud limitation.

izzy: Engineering notes: propose a "manifest-envelope" format (v1) that includes fields {version, cloud-hints, ip-preserve: boolean, sig, checksums}. We'll ship an example manifest and a tiny validator binary.

yara: Good. For handover flow, I want a one-line netops brief that says: what we will change, expected minutes of interruption (if any), and the exact list of IPs to verify post-upgrade. Make it easily copy-pasteable into their ticket system.

owen: For upgrades: operator to support a `pause-point` annotation where the control-plane can be canaried, pause for KV warm, and then continue. We'll expose a `--pause-timeout` and a `--rollback-marker` label so automation can detect failures.

izzy: Offline installs: signed tarball + envelope.json + verify.sh. verify.sh will check signatures and output a CSV of endpoints and their IPs before/after. We'll include an example output to show customers.

claire: Security: tokenized peering exchange should be TTL-limited (suggest 1h), and we must provide least-privilege IAM snippets for common cloud providers. Also document KMS patterns for BYO-KMS and where to put audit-log endpoints.

yara: Customer acceptance criteria (compact):
- Manifest-envelope + signed tarball received
- Peering token exchanged and peering applied
- `verify.sh` run with IP-delta == 0 (for IP-preserve path) or delta documented
- Customer confirms runbook receipt + SME contact card
If any step fails -> pause and escalate to engineering.

owen: UX ask: create a 1/2-page quickstart titled "netops one-liner" that contains the copy-pasteable handoff + the exact kubectl commands to run verify.sh. Keep it < 12 lines.

izzy: I'll draft the envelope schema and the validator + verify.sh. I'll also add a sample `rollback-marker` watcher snippet:
```
# sample watcher
kubectl annotate ns redwood upgrade-phase=canary
watch -n 5 kubectl get pods -l app=redwood-operator -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.phase}'
```

yara: Field will want an email template + a playbook that lists who we call if peering fails (SME card). Add a short 'what to collect' log bundle command (one-liner that collects operator logs + manifest).

claire: Launch gates proposal (compact):
- Envelope v1 spec + example manifest published
- Signed installer artifact + offline tarball available (checksums verified)
- Tokenized peering flow documented with IAM snippets
- verify.sh and validator published with sample outputs
- Netops one-liner + SME contact card + support playbook
If any item not met -> label as "limited GA" and require field enablement.

ops-bot: Created ticket RDW-PL-46011 "Minimal handover package: VPC/on-prem"  assignees: @izzy @owen @yara. ETA: 7bd.

yara: I'll author the netops brief and SME contact card draft and post in /docs/private/handoffs.

izzy: I'll drop the envelope schema + validator PR and ping this thread.

owen: I'll build the peering-token guide and the IAM snippets.

claire: Nice work. Let's pick this up in Tues' sync. If anyone hits a blocker, raise a short note and tag #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
